nodes.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach.

A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter that sorts messages into folders, then uses the classifier in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages for misclassification.

A model generated during the first pass of the multi-pass message filter, maintained exclusively in non-persistent memory on a user's client device and not stored on disk or in any persistent data store.

A message filter configured to sort messages into different message folders and store first classification data in a persistent store.<SEP>A previously applied message filter that sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store.<SEP>A message filter that sorts messages into different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store; it is automatically executed independent of user action.

A filter configured to generate a classification model based on a first pass analysis, perform a second pass on sorted messages to generate misclassification identification, and be trained based on which folder each message resides.

A device distinct from a client device on which the first message filter is configured to execute.<SEP>A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform first and second pass analyses, display misclassification identification, and purge the classification model from non-persistent memory.<SEP>A device configured to receive messages, assign them to message folders using the first message filter, and communicate the messages over a network.
A component of the network device that sends and receives data over a network.
A component of the network device operative to perform actions including first pass analysis, second pass analysis, displaying misclassification identification, and purging the classification model.

A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter, used to train the multi-pass message filter.<SEP>Different folders into which messages are sorted; a message may be identified as sorted into an incorrect message folder and moved to another folder by a user.
An identification of sorted messages that might be misclassified, generated by the second pass and displayed so that misclassified messages can be moved to a different folder.
A memory location where the generated classification model resides exclusively, from which the model is purged and not stored on disk or another persistent data store.
A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A persistent data store where the first message filter stores first classification data.

A storage medium storing instructions that, when executed, perform operations including the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter.<SEP>A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages.

A device on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may execute entirely, and on which the first pass is executed.<SEP>A user's device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may occur entirely.<SEP>A device on which the multi-pass message filter is executed, holding second classification data exclusively in a non-persistent memory store and providing a display of information to a user.
Information within messages read during the first pass, including sender address and whether the sender's address is in an address book associated with a recipient.
Information within messages read during the first pass, including a subject and an originating network address.
The contents of messages read during the first pass analysis.
Attachments within messages read during the first pass analysis.

An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used in analysis to generate the classification model.<SEP>An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders; a message sender's address in it may be analyzed to generate second classification data.
Classification data stored in a persistent store by the first message filter.<SEP>Classification data generated by the first message filter and stored in a persistent store.

Classification data generated during the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train the filter; it can be deleted so that it is no longer accessible.<SEP>Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter, residing exclusively in a non-persistent memory store and used to score messages in the second pass.<SEP>Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train it; it resides exclusively in a non-persistent memory store and is used to score messages.
A score assigned to each message by the second pass of the multi-pass message filter, used to identify messages sorted into an incorrect folder.

A message filtering system that executes a first pass and a second pass to classify messages, optionally employing a Naive Bayes classifier, and can run entirely on a client device or partly on a network device.<SEP>A message filter executed in multiple passes on a client device; a first pass trains the filter by generating second classification data, and a second pass uses that data to score each message.
A classifier that the multi-pass message filter may employ.
A model generated based on analysis of at least which message folder a message currently resides.
One of a plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted, and whose contents may be analyzed to generate the second classification model.

A method for managing message delivery comprising receiving messages, sorting them into folders using a first message filter, and executing a first pass of a multi-pass message filter on a client device.
A memory store on the client device where second classification data resides exclusively and from which it is deleted upon providing the display of information.
A plurality of messages received, sorted into message folders, and scored by the multi-pass message filter.
A communications network over which messages are communicated to message folders.
A person enabled to move an identified message to another message folder and able to select execution of the multi-pass message filter through an interface.
An interface on the client device through which a user can select execution of the multi-pass message filter.
A header of a message that may be analyzed to generate second classification data.
The content of a message that may be analyzed to generate second classification data.
